questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using an Inverse Matrix With Reorganization
questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x=5y \\ x=-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-5y=0 \\ x=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 0-(-5)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+y=0 \\ 3x-6y=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot (-6)-1\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-6 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}-6 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}-6 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=7 \\ 8x+y=7\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 8 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 8 & 1\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+2y=1 \\ 2x-3y=-2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot (-3)-2\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3=y \\ 3y=4x+2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=3 \\ -4x+3y=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-(-4)\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
